title: Outer .otherwise() containing a nested when corrupts outer branch metadata (reports wrong taken_branch/index/dimmed)
description: In _BranchTrackingEvaluator._eval_clauses, the `then` path sets `self._is_outer = False` (line 2094) before recursing into the then value, but the `otherwise` path (lines 2107-2113) sets taken_branch/taken_branch_index/dimmed_branches WITHOUT clearing `self._is_outer`. So when the outer `.otherwise()` value itself contains a nested when-chain, `self.evaluate(clause['otherwise'])` (line 2113) recurses into the inner chain's _eval_clauses with `is_outer = self._is_outer` still True. The inner chain then overwrites taken_branch/taken_branch_index/dimmed_branches with ITS OWN (inner) values, clobbering the outer's. The trace therefore reports that the outer THEN clause fired when in fact the outer OTHERWISE fired. This metadata is serialized verbatim into step.calculation via dataclasses.asdict(evaluated) (_trace_enrichment.py:1523) and drives which clause the explainability UI highlights/dims, so the user is shown the wrong branch as taken.
evidence: Executed repro (polars 1.39.2). Code: out=pl.when(pl.col('a')>0).then(99).otherwise(pl.when(pl.col('b')>0).then(1).otherwise(2)); row a=-1,b=1. _compute_result_impl returns 1 (correct: outer-otherwise -> inner-then). But _evaluate_conditional_branches returns {'taken_branch':'then','taken_branch_index':0,'dimmed_branches':[1],'nested_branches':[]} — claiming the outer THEN (value 99, index 0) was taken, which is false; the outer OTHERWISE (index 1) fired. Root cause: otherwise branch lacks the `self._is_outer = False` that the then branch has at line 2094, so the nested evaluate() overwrites the just-set outer metadata.
